To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a single breath-held GRE sequence can be used to measure cardiac and liver T2* in most children and young adults with iron overload.
liver and myocardial T2* measurements can be performed with a single breath-held acquisition and that there is a good correlation between these measurements.
liver T2* can reliably be measured from cardiac MRI examinations, and vice versa, and that this can be accomplished on a single breath hold.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a new MRI technique that will be used to measure the T2* relaxation time of both the liver and the heart in the same breath-hold.
the measurement of liver iron concentration in children with sickle cell disease.
the development and evaluation of a new method for the determination of the T2* relaxation time of the liver and myocardium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the liver T2* measurement on the cardiac MRI is as accurate as that on the dedicated liver MRI.
the liver and myocardium iron concentrations can be measured on the same single breath-hold MRI examination in most patients with suspected and known iron overload.
a single breath-holt multi-echo GRE acquisition is sufficient for measuring liver and cardiac T2*, with the exception of a few patients with extreme iron overload.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the T2* values obtained from the liver and the myocardium are highly correlated, with only a small mean bias, and that a single breath-holt acquisition can be used for both.
the cardiac MRI examination may be used as a surrogate for liver T2* in patients with known or suspected liver iron overload.
a single breath-held GRE sequence may provide sufficient information for evaluation of both liver and cardiac iron overload.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in patients who require both cardiac and liver MRI, a single acquisition can provide both measurements.
the same sequence can be used for both liver and cardiac T2*.
in patients with suspected or confirmed liver iron overload, a dedicated liver MRI is not needed to measure cardiac iron.
